info.title: Competitor catalog API
info.description:
Competitor catalog scraper API: competitors and their worker (catalog sync / price
refresh / product matching), scraped categories, products and price history, runs,
matching of competitor products with the reference catalog (Antalis), notifications.

Authentication: send the API key in the `X-API-Key` header (or `Authorization: Bearer`).
MCP server (every endpoint as a tool): `POST /api/v1/mcp?api_key=<key>` (Streamable HTTP).
Errors: `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}`. Full guide: `docs/api/` in the repository.

get.summary: Liveness of the API, database and worker
get.description:
No authentication. ``worker.online`` is false when the worker process has not sent a
heartbeat for 60 s: jobs can still be queued but will not start until it is back.
Proxied from Scrape.do (limited by Scrape.do to 10 calls per minute).

get.description:
``daily``: one row per day of the period (zeros included). ``price_position``: per
non-reference competitor, over the associated pairs (auto_matched or validated, both
products active) whose latest from prices are comparable: same currency, both the price of
one sales unit (unit basis, unit quantity 1 or unknown), tax modes not known to differ.
gap = (competitor - antalis) / antalis * 100; ``same`` = |gap| < 1.

post.summary: Start the worker on a task (catalog_sync, price_refresh or matching)
post.description:
Queues a job; the worker process picks it up within a few seconds.

Refusals (HTTP 409): ``worker_busy`` (the competitor already has a queued/running job,
whatever its task), ``catalog_required`` (price refresh or matching before any full
catalog sync), ``competitor_disabled``; matching only: ``matching_reference`` (the
reference catalog itself), ``reference_catalog_required``, ``reference_missing``,
``matching_not_configured`` (no VOYAGE_API_KEY).

post.summary: Stop the active job of the competitor
post.description:
A queued job is cancelled at once; a running job stops after the current page
(``state`` becomes ``stopping``, then the job ends as ``cancelled``).

post.summary: Pause the running job (resumable)
post.description:
The job pauses after the current page (``state``: ``pausing`` then ``paused``) and keeps
its place and the competitor's worker slot: no other task can start until it is resumed or
stopped. A paused job does not survive a worker restart/redeploy (it ends ``interrupted``).

post.summary: Resume a paused job
post.description: ``state`` becomes ``resuming`` then ``running`` within a few seconds.

post.summary: Estimate the duration/credits of a task without starting it

post.summary: Cancel a job
Pause a running job
Resume a paused job
Restart an interrupted, failed or cancelled job where it stopped
post.description:
Queues a new job of the same task (``resumed_from_job_id`` = this job) that skips the
work already done: a catalog sync replays the category pages already fetched (no request)
and does not refetch the products synced since the stopped job started, a price refresh
skips the products priced since then, a matching is incremental anyway. Jobs interrupted by a worker restart
are restarted automatically (``requested_by: "auto_resume"``) unless the server sets
``WORKER_AUTO_RESUME=false``.

post.summary: Unban a category: recreate it (empty), optionally queue its catalog sync
post.description:
The category is recreated with its saved metadata (name, URL, external id, kind, parent)
under a **new id**, without sub-categories nor products: they come back with a catalog sync of
the category (``scrape: true``, or ``POST /categories/{id}/scrape`` later) or the next full
sync. With ``scrape: true`` the unban is refused as a whole when the sync cannot be queued
(``worker_busy``, ``competitor_disabled``...).

delete.description:
Its products and sub-categories are kept, detached (``category_id``/``parent_id`` set to null).
A later catalog sync recreates it if it still exists on the site.

post.summary: Ban a category: delete it with its subtree and skip it in every crawl
post.description:
Deletes the category, all its sub-categories, their products with their price history,
their matches and match history. Matches of other competitors associated with a deleted
(reference) product become ``deprecated``. Only the category's own metadata is kept (the
returned ban), to recreate it with ``POST /categories/banned/{ban_id}/unban``. Catalog syncs
skip the category, every page below it and every product whose navigation path contains it.

Refusals (HTTP 409): ``worker_busy`` (the competitor has an active job), ``matching_running``
(a category of the reference catalog while a matching job runs).

post.summary: Catalog sync of this category only (sub-categories, products, prices)
post.description:
Queues a ``catalog_sync`` job with ``options.category_id``: the crawl starts from the
category's URL and follows its whole subtree, even when the category is empty in the
database (e.g. just unbanned). Banned sub-categories stay skipped. Never a full sync: nothing
is flagged missing. Same refusals as ``POST /competitors/{key}/worker/start``.

post.summary: Match the products of this category only
post.description:
Queues a ``matching`` job with ``options.category_id``: only the competitor's products
of this category and its sub-categories are (re)matched, against the whole reference
catalog. Same refusals as ``POST /matching/competitors/{key}/run`` (a category of the
reference catalog itself is refused with ``matching_reference``).

post.summary: Retry only the pages that failed in a run
post.description:
Queues a job on the run's competitor that refetches only the failed pages of the run:
a ``catalog_sync`` with ``retry_failed_run_id`` for a catalog run (failed product pages,
including products never created, and failed listing pages with their sub-pages), a
``price_refresh`` with ``retry_failed_run_id`` for a price refresh run. ``409
nothing_to_retry`` when the run has no failed page; ``worker_busy`` as usual.

Counts per status, products never matched, items to review, deprecated matches,
whether a run can start (prerequisites: full catalog sync of the competitor and of the
reference catalog, VOYAGE_API_KEY), the active/last matching job. The reference
competitor is not listed.

post.summary: Match the products of a competitor
post.description:
Queues a matching job (followed like any job: ``GET /jobs/{id}``, worker endpoints,
notifications). Default mode ``incremental``: what changed since the last run only.
Whatever the mode, texts already embedded are never sent to Voyage AI again unless
``reembed`` is true: rerunning ``mode=all`` after a scoring change costs no embedding.

Refusals (HTTP 409): ``matching_reference``, ``catalog_required`` (no full catalog sync of
the competitor yet: its products are not parsed), ``reference_catalog_required``,
``reference_missing``, ``matching_not_configured``, ``worker_busy``, ``competitor_disabled``.
At the end, a ``matching_summary`` notification gives the number of products to review.

post.summary: Recompute every deprecated match
post.description:
Queues one ``mode=deprecated`` matching job per competitor that has deprecated matches
(nothing else is recomputed). Competitors whose worker is busy are reported in ``refused``.

get.description:

(by a human, ``manual_choice`` when another product was chosen), ``needs_review``,
``no_match``, ``rejected`` (a human confirmed there is no equivalent), ``deprecated``.

get.description:
Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`) for the console. Named events, JSON in `data:`:

* `console.summary` (ConsoleSummary): sent on connect, then whenever any part changes.
* `job.updated` (Job): any change of an active job (at most ~1/s per job), and job creation.
* `job.finished` (Job): the job reached succeeded, partial, failed, cancelled or interrupted.
* `notification.created` (Notification).
* `matching.updated` (MatchingSummary): a competitor whose match counts changed.
* `competitor.updated` (Competitor): worker state or sync timestamps changed.

Comment heartbeat `: ping` every 15 s, `retry: 3000`. Changes are detected by polling the
database every second: an event arrives up to ~1 s after the change. A client that cannot
keep up is disconnected (it reconnects and gets a fresh `console.summary`).
